chunks: From him, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said:

I gathered myself in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be your ransom! Sometimes I feel grief without a calamity befalling me or a matter descending upon me, to the extent that my family and my close friend recognize that in my face.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, O Jabir! Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the believers from the clay of Paradise and caused a spirit from His Spirit to flow among them. Therefore, the believer is a brother to the believer, like his father and mother. So if a spirit from those spirits in a city from the cities is struck by grief, this one is grieved because it is from them.'
ai.seo_question: Why do believers feel each other's grief and sorrow according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Jabir al-Ju'fi recounts his experience of unexplained grief to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who elucidates the metaphysical bond of believers through the concept of 'clay of Paradise' (Tinat al-Jinan). This spiritual kinship implies that believers share a single soul or essence, causing the emotional state of one to resonate with others, thereby reinforcing the practical implication of mutual empathy in Shia ethics. The narration highlights how this intrinsic connection transcends physical distance, making the grief of any believer a shared burden for the community.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban, from Jabir Al Ju’fy who said,

‘I felt uneasy in front of Abu Ja’farasws, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Sometimes I panic from without there being a difficulty hitting me, or a matter descending upon me to the extent my family and my friends recognise that in my face’. So heasws said: ‘Yes, O Jabir! Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Created the Momineen from the clay of Paradise, and Caused a spirit from Hisazwj Spirit to flow among them. Thus, due to that, the Momin is a brother of the Momin, of his father and his mother. Therefore, if a spirit from those spirits, in a city from the cities, were to be struck by grief, this one would (also) be grieved because it is from these’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Amr ibn Aban from Jabir al-Juhfi who has said the following:

“Once I became depressed in the presence of abu Ja’far (a.s.) and asked him, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, why is it that sometimes I feel depressed without any apparent cause or incident? Even my family and friends notice it on my face.’ The Imam said, ‘Yes O Jabir, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has created the clay of the believers from the clay of paradise and has made the fragrance of His spirit flow through it; thus, a believer is a brother (in belief) of a believer from his father and mother. When a spirit of those spirits is distressed anywhere with a sadness the other spirits also feel sad; this is from that (clay of paradise).”’
